grading_method: Evaluator manually compared every requested material part of each answer with the fixed source-backed key and frozen summary; support labels did not determine grades. Key details not requested by question are not mandatory.

grades.question: How are Factory cards, encounter tokens, and the structure bonus set up, and who starts?
grades.expected_answer: Shuffle Factory cards; select players+1 face-down and return others unseen to box. Put an encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly select one face-up structure bonus tile. Lowest numbered Player Mat starts, then clockwise.
grades.observed_answer: Shuffle the Factory deck, randomly select players + 1 cards face-down onto the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: “number of players + 1”; “11 marked territories”; “lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.”
grades.reason: Factory selection/count/unseen return, 11 encounters, random face-up tile and lowest-mat starter resolved.

grades.question: What starts on the map and each mat, and which mat supplies starting power, combat cards, popularity, coins and objectives?
grades.expected_answer: Character on own home base; one worker on each of two land-adjoined territories. Faction Mat supplies power/combat cards, holds four mechs and six stars. Player Mat supplies popularity/coins/objectives, holds six technology cubes on black-square green boxes, four structures, four recruits and remaining six workers on Produce; action token starts beside it.
grades.observed_answer: The character starts at the home base; two workers start one on each of the two land-adjoined territories adjoining it; four mechs go over the Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in green Player Mat boxes marked with a black square; four structures in matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits on the bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; and the action token beside the Player Mat, ready for first placement. Leave faction one-time recruit spaces empty. The Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; the Player Mat sets popularity, coins, and two objective cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup steps 3–4 enumerate mat assignments and all starting pieces.
grades.reason: Map and mat pieces, action-token starting location and correct assignment of starting values resolved.

grades.question: May you skip both actions, repeat a section, use top-row gains below, or take the bottom action first? How are costs and benefits determined?
grades.expected_answer: Must move token to different section, except Rusviet may repeat including Factory. Top then bottom, each optional once; may skip both. May use top gains below. Pay full exposed red-box cost before taking as much or as little exposed green benefit as desired.
grades.observed_answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action, either one, or both. If taking both, top must precede bottom. Rusviet may repeat a section, including its Factory card. Top-row gains can pay a bottom-row cost. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before the action; then choose as much or as little of the exposed green-box benefit as desired. Exact bottom-row resource costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: “different section”; “full cost”; “as much or as little”; top-row gains may pay bottom-row cost.
grades.reason: Mandatory token move, optional actions/ordering, Rusviet exception, top gains below, exposed full costs/optional gains resolved.

grades.question: Who controls a structure territory occupied by an enemy worker, who can use the structure, and from where may you spend resources for an action elsewhere?
grades.expected_answer: Enemy worker controls territory and resources; structure owner retains abilities except cannot Produce at an uncontrolled Mill; enemy gains no structure ability. Spend resources from any controlled territories for actions anywhere; spent resources go to supply.
grades.observed_answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls that territory and all its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure’s abilities; you keep those abilities without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Pay action resource costs from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
grades.reader_evidence: Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker controls its territory; “You keep those abilities even without control”; pay from “any territories you currently control.”
grades.reason: Enemy worker control, owner-only persistent structure ability/Mill exception and remote resource spending resolved.

grades.question: On a normal unupgraded Move, can one unit move twice, can a transported worker subsequently move, and who can carry what?
grades.expected_answer: Move up to two different units one adjacent territory each, sequentially, or gain $1 instead. All units carry any number of resources; only mechs carry any number of own workers, not characters. Carriage is not the worker movement so worker can subsequently move itself.
grades.observed_answer: No. Normal Move allows up to two different units one adjacent territory each, and the same unit cannot use both selections to move twice. Being carried does not count as a worker’s own movement, so a transported worker may subsequently move itself. All units (characters, mechs, workers) can carry any number of resources; only mechs may additionally carry any number of your workers, never your character.
grades.reader_evidence: Move OR coins: “two different units”; “cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice”; “Being carried does not count”; only mechs carry workers.
grades.reason: Distinct-unit movement, transported worker own movement and all resource/mech worker transport restrictions resolved.

grades.question: What happens when a Speed-enabled mech enters enemy workers only, even at zero popularity; may its workers enter that territory by themselves?
grades.expected_answer: Mech stops and cannot move again this turn. Enemy workers immediately retreat home leaving resources; attacker loses one popularity each to minimum zero, still retreats them. Workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
grades.observed_answer: The Speed-enabled mech entering a territory with enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn. The workers immediately retreat to their home base, leave resources behind, and you lose one popularity per worker, down to zero; insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. It is not combat. Your workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: enemy workers immediately retreat; lose “one popularity per worker, down to zero”; worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
grades.reason: Enemy-worker-only stop, immediate home retreat/resources, popularity floor and independent worker-entry restriction resolved.

grades.question: When does combat occur after movement, who chooses multiple combat order, and can workers enter or leave enemy-character/mech-controlled territory alone?
grades.expected_answer: Finish all movement, then combats before bottom-row action. Active attacker chooses order. Attacking plastic unit stops on entry and enemy temporarily controls territory. Workers cannot enter or leave such territory independently.
grades.observed_answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve any combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: “Finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action”; “attacker chooses multiple-combat order.”
grades.reason: Combat after all movement/before bottom, attacker ordering and independent worker enter/leave prohibition resolved.

grades.question: State Bolster and Trade costs and choices; where are traded resources placed and what if all workers are home? What if the combat deck is exhausted?
grades.expected_answer: Bolster $1 for 2 power OR 1 combat card; Trade $1 for any two resources OR 1 popularity. Place resources on controlled territory with worker; cannot trade for resources with all workers home. Empty combat deck reshuffles discards; if both empty draw none.
grades.observed_answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card (before upgrades); a built Monument also gives one popularity. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards to form a new deck; if both deck and discard are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources, same or different, or one popularity (before upgrades); a built Armory also gives one power. Traded resources go on a controlled territory with at least one worker. If all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
grades.reader_evidence: Bolster and Trade sections state costs, choices, building bonuses, placement, and empty-deck handling.
grades.reason: Both $1 top-action choices, worker-controlled trade placement/home prohibition and deck exhaustion branches resolved.

grades.question: How is Produce paid and resolved, where do new workers come from, can benefits be declined, and do new workers change the cost already paid?
grades.expected_answer: Pay all exposed red costs before action, must afford full power/popularity/coins. Choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker may produce one terrain token there. Villages produce workers from Player Mat left to right, after payment, so new exposure affects future Produce costs. May decline production/workers. Workers never return to mat.
grades.observed_answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that same territory. New workers are taken from the Player Mat left to right after payment and placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Newly exposed costs affect future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce steps 1–3: pay in full, choose up to two territories, and take workers after payment; “You may decline.”
grades.reason: Full exposed pre-payment, terrain production, left-to-right village workers, optional benefits and future-cost timing resolved.

grades.question: What are Upgrade and Deploy costs, placement restrictions and effects, and can a completed bottom action still be paid?
grades.expected_answer: Upgrade oil: cube from any green box to empty bracketed red box, never solid border. Deploy metal: choose mech on Faction Mat, put on controlled worker territory, never lake; uncovered ability applies to character/all mechs, not workers. Costs/coins vary by mat. Completed bottom action may still be paid for coins and applicable recruit bonus.
grades.observed_answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes. Both amounts vary by mat and upgrades. Upgrade moves a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy places a mech from the Faction Mat on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake; its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after all upgrades, mechs, structures, or recruits are completed, you may still pay for the bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade, Deploy, and continued payment after completing pieces are stated explicitly.
grades.reason: Correct costs, cube-transfer restrictions, Deploy effect and completed-action payment, but the question expressly asks Upgrade effects and this answer never explains that removing the cube improves a top benefit and placing it reduces a bottom cost. Correct mechanics alone leave that requested effect unstated; there is no contradiction. Independent expanded02-adjudication.json.

grades.question: Where may a structure be built, can it move or be destroyed, and how do Mill and Mine work when their territories are occupied by enemies?
grades.expected_answer: Build costs wood, controlled worker territory, one structure total per territory; Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden. Permanent cannot move/destroy. Mill adds bonus Produce territory and produces as worker plus actual workers only while controlled. Mine personal tunnel usable for all unit movement even enemy-controlled, enemy cannot use it.
grades.observed_answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory with your worker; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden. Only one structure total may be on a territory, including opponents’ structures. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A Mill provides its bonus production territory only while you control it; an enemy unit can remove your control, so it then cannot produce. A Mine is your personal tunnel for your unit movement, including Factory Move, even when enemy-controlled; the ability remains yours despite lack of control. Opponents cannot use your structure abilities.
grades.reader_evidence: Build: placement and permanence; Mill works “only while controlled”; Mine is personal and works “even when enemy-controlled.”
grades.reason: Worker/control structure placement, single-structure/terrain restrictions, permanence and enemy-control Mill/Mine exceptions resolved.

grades.question: When enlisting, where does the token go, what are the one-time bonuses, which action sets ongoing bonus, and how do simultaneous/two-player bonuses resolve?
grades.expected_answer: Pay food; remove any recruit from Player Mat, permanently place on open Faction one-time space for 2 power/coins/popularity/combat cards. Ongoing bonus linked to section uncovered, triggered by self or immediate left/right taking that bottom action, not top/Factory. Announce actions. Active then left then right; sixth star immediately ends. In 2-player opponent triggers once.
grades.observed_answer: Put the recruited token permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus space on your Faction Mat and immediately gain two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards (your choice). The ongoing bonus is determined by the Player Mat circle uncovered where the recruit was removed: Upgrade gives one power, Deploy one coin, Build one popularity, Enlist one combat card. Resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
grades.reader_evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits specify placement, four one-time benefits, action-based ongoing benefit, and resolution order.
grades.reason: Permanent open Faction placement, four one-time choices, uncovered-section ongoing trigger, active-left-right and two-player exception resolved.

grades.question: What may each combatant secretly spend on dial and cards, how do combat abilities resolve, and how are totals paid and ties broken?
grades.expected_answer: May fight at zero power/popularity. Attacker mech ability first, then defender. Dial 0 to min(current power,7). Up to one card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial. Reveal simultaneously; add card values, attacker wins tie. Both pay dial power and discard used cards face-up; card values do not reduce track.
grades.observed_answer: Each combatant secretly and simultaneously chooses dial power from 0 to the smaller of seven and current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even at zero dial power; Rusviet People’s Army adds one card if any workers are present. Combat abilities are used attacker first, then defender, if both have abilities. Reveal dials/cards simultaneously, add dial and card values, and attacker wins ties. Both players lose their dial power from their tracks and discard every played card face-up; card values do not reduce track power.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 1–3 give simultaneous secret choices, card limits, ability order, payment, and attacker wins ties.
grades.reason: Capped dial/card spending, attacker-first abilities, simultaneous reveal/tie, both dial payments and used-card face-up discard resolved.

grades.question: After combat, what happens to all units/resources, popularity, combat stars, and the losing player combat-card reward?
grades.expected_answer: Winner controls territory/resources, places combat star if below two (Saxony unlimited available stars), may still fight after limit. Loser retreats all units including workers home leaving resources. Winning attacker loses one popularity per opposing worker retreated; winning defender does not. Loser draws one combat card if revealed at least one power on dial OR cards, none for zero total.
grades.observed_answer: The winner controls the territory and its resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally up to two; Saxony has no usual limit within six available). All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy permits eligible units and carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Polania Camaraderie provides its stated aggressor combat exception. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 4–5 state retreats, resources, popularity, combat stars and loser card reward.
grades.reason: Winner control/star limit, all-unit retreat/resources, attacker/defender popularity and dial-or-card loser reward resolved.

grades.question: When is an encounter resolved after contested entry, what if the character loses, where do gains go, and do normal action costs/bonuses apply?
grades.expected_answer: Character stops/cannot move again on entering token; finish Move and all combats before bottom action, only if character still there (must win contested entry). If loses token stays. Discard token, draw encounter, choose one affordable option (Polania up to two); pay printed cost and may decline benefits. Resources/structures/mechs/workers go to encounter territory. No additional normal costs/benefits or recruit bonuses; card face-down bottom encounter deck.
grades.observed_answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory; discard the token and draw a card before any following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. All resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay no additional normal action costs and receive no additional mat benefits, including ongoing recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Encounters: after Move and all combats; contested loss leaves token; gains go to encounter territory; no normal action costs or mat benefits.
grades.reason: After-Move/all-combat encounter eligibility, losing-character token persistence, benefit destination and isolated costs/bonuses resolved.

grades.question: Who takes a Factory card, when, may later visitors take one or change theirs, and how do Factory actions and Speed movement differ from mat actions?
grades.expected_answer: Each character first finishing Move at Factory after any combat must choose one available card, return rest; not just first visitor, max one permanent card per player, cannot exchange. Fifth section, optional top then bottom; no corresponding mat coins/structure/recruit bonuses. Bottom Move one unit up to twice (three with character/mech Speed), same stop rules, Mine usable.
grades.observed_answer: Every player’s character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), looks at the available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. A Factory card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom, subject to the normal no-repeat rule except Rusviet. Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories in that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and normal movement and stop rules apply.
grades.reader_evidence: Factory section states each player's first visit, permanent card, action and movement rules.
grades.reason: Every character first-visit eligibility, after-Move choice, one permanent card, independent Factory bonuses and Speed/normal movement resolved.

grades.question: When can an objective be revealed, what requirements and discards apply, and what changes for Saxony?
grades.expected_answer: Only own turn before/after complete top or bottom action, all requirements true at reveal; may delay reveal. Place one objective star, discard both objectives to deck bottom. Saxony keeps second and may complete both, unrestricted combat/objective stars within six available.
grades.observed_answer: Only on your own turn, before or after a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; you may wait, but must meet all requirements at reveal. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of the deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed. Saxony keeps the other card after the first and may complete both starting objectives and score both.
grades.reader_evidence: Objectives and agreements: own turn timing, requirements at reveal, both cards discarded to bottom, Saxony exception.
grades.reason: Own-turn complete-action timing, all requirements at reveal, deck-bottom discards and Saxony keep/score second resolved; specific card text was not requested.

grades.question: Which achievements earn stars, may stars be lost or another player block a goal, and when does the game end?
grades.expected_answer: Six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, eight workers on board, completed objective, up to two combat victories, 18 popularity,16 power. Must place on achievement, each once except combat two/Saxony exception; irreversible and other players may share goals. Sixth star ends immediately, no extra turns/actions.
grades.observed_answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony’s exception. Stars are permanent even if power or popularity later drops, and another player’s star never blocks your goal. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars and immediate end lists achievements, permanence, no blocking, and immediate sixth-star end.
grades.reason: All star achievements, permanence, shared goals and immediate sixth-star termination resolved.

grades.question: If a bottom action earns the sixth star, what is collected first; what happens to pending battles and a neighbor recruit star?
grades.expected_answer: Gain primary benefit, coins and own recruit ongoing benefit before placing bottom-action sixth star. Undo movement into any still-unresolved battle, return units to origin. Neighbor power/popularity star from recruit only after active action, in order active/left/right (clockwise), only if active did not already end game; stop remaining events at sixth star.
grades.observed_answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect the primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and return initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat. For neighbors’ power/popularity recruit stars, finish the active action, then resolve active player first, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for a sixth star at each step; after a sixth star, no later recruit star or bonus resolves.
grades.reader_evidence: Sixth-star sequence spells out bottom-action collection, pending battle undo, and neighbor recruit order.
grades.reason: Pre-star bottom benefits, pending-battle rollback and neighbor recruit priority/interruption resolved.

grades.question: At 10 popularity, how much do 5 stars, 4 normal territories plus Factory, and 13 resources add to held coins? Include structure bonus eligibility and all victory tiebreakers.
grades.expected_answer: Tier 7-12 pays $4/star,$3/territory,$2/resource pair. 5 stars=$20; 4+Factory as 3=7 territories=$21; six pairs=$12, total $53 plus held coins and structure tile. Structure bonus even without control. Most coins wins; ties workers+mechs+structures (not character), power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, placed stars.
grades.observed_answer: At 10 popularity, the table’s 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per controlled territory, and $2 per complete pair of controlled resources: 5 stars = $20; four ordinary territories plus Factory (five territories for scoring) = $15; 13 resources = six pairs = $12. These add $47 to held coins (the summary’s example says $53, but its displayed arithmetic is $20 + $21 + $12, treating territories as seven; that example conflicts with the stated prompt’s four ordinary plus Factory, which is five total territories). The selected structure bonus is also scored, even if enemies control your structures’ territories. Tiebreakers: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, then stars placed.
grades.reader_evidence: Final fortune table gives 7–12 payouts; Factory counts as three territories total; structure bonus remains eligible; tiebreak order listed. Example says “$20 + $21 + $12 = $53.”
grades.reason: Factory is three scoring territories total. Four ordinary territories plus Factory score as seven territories: $20 stars + $21 territories + $12 complete resource pairs = $53. Both instead explicitly count five and return $47, materially contradicting the Factory rule despite otherwise correct structure eligibility and tiebreakers. Independent expanded02-adjudication.json.

grades.question: Is a home base a territory, may you enter one normally, and are expansion home bases active?
grades.expected_answer: Home base is not territory for any game effect; cannot normally move back in, build/deploy there. Starts and forced retreat exceptions; Crimea Wayfare explicit movement exception. Two unrepresented bases are expansion placeholders/inactive.
grades.observed_answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move back into a home base, build there, or deploy there; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea’s unlocked Wayfare. Expansion placeholder bases without matching core factions are inactive.
grades.reader_evidence: Control, resources and home bases: “A home base is not a territory”; default restrictions and inactive placeholders.
grades.reason: Non-territory home base/default prohibitions, explicit exceptions and inactive expansion placeholders resolved.

grades.question: Which terrain produces each token, do Factory/lake produce, are workers resources, and what happens if resource supply runs out?
grades.expected_answer: Mountain metal; tundra oil; farm food; forest wood; village workers. Lake/Factory nothing. Workers not resources. Resource supply unlimited; use multipliers as necessary, no territory token/unit limit.
grades.observed_answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers. Lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce terrain table and resources section: workers are not resources; resource tokens have no supply limit.
grades.reason: All terrain outputs/no-output spaces, nonresource workers, unlimited resources and territory quantities resolved.

grades.question: May resources be picked up/dropped mid-movement, can mechs carry characters, and what does unlocked Speed change about tunnels and stops?
grades.expected_answer: All units may pick/drop any resources; mechs also own workers, never character. Speed adds one territory for character/mechs, including before/after tunnel jump which costs one move; may pick/drop mid-move. Entering enemy unit ends movement/cannot move again turn; character encounter also stops.
grades.observed_answer: All units can pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources during movement; a mech can also carry any number of your workers mid-movement, but never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, so the extra step may be before or after it. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
grades.reader_evidence: Move section states resource carriage, mech worker carriage, Speed and tunnel-step rules.
grades.reason: All-unit resource pickup/drop, mech own-worker/no-character carriage, Speed/tunnel step and overriding stops resolved.

grades.question: Can workers capture a territory controlled only by an enemy structure, and are printed tunnels usable by all unit types?
grades.expected_answer: Yes any unit may enter structure-only territory and controls it; no combat from structure alone. All printed tunnel territories adjacent for Move by any unit; enemy Mine not a public tunnel.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: “Any unit may enter” enemy-structure-only territory; “All printed tunnel territories are adjacent” for any unit.
grades.reason: Any unit captures enemy structure-only territory, no structure combat, all-unit printed tunnels versus personal Mine resolved.

grades.question: If unable to afford any action after last using Move, must you pay a partial Produce cost or what turn is legal?
grades.expected_answer: Never partial payment; full cost required. Take a dead turn choosing another section with no actions, still moving token.
grades.observed_answer: You never pay only part of a cost. If you cannot afford any action, take a dead turn: move the token to a different section and take neither action. Since you last used Move, select a different section as usual; no partial Produce payment is legal.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: “Never pay only part of a cost”; unaffordable actions permit a dead turn by moving to a different section.
grades.reason: Full payment required; legal dead turn shifts token and takes neither action resolved.

grades.question: What do Armory and Monument grant, when do those benefits trigger, and can an enemy occupant take them away?
grades.expected_answer: Armory adds 1 power when owner takes Trade, Monument adds 1 popularity when owner takes Bolster. Uncovered benefits apply future respective top actions, regardless territory control; opponent never gains them. Factory similar actions excluded.
grades.observed_answer: A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These trigger as part of those actions. You retain structure abilities even without control, so an enemy occupant does not take them away; the exception is that an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce.
grades.reader_evidence: Bolster/Trade building bonuses; control section says abilities remain without control except Mill production.
grades.reason: Trade Armory power/Bolster Monument popularity, future triggering and owner persistence versus enemy control resolved.

grades.question: How does each base faction Riverwalk differ, which units receive it, and does Nordic Swim give lake movement or help its mechs?
grades.expected_answer: Riverwalk only character/mechs: Saxony and Nordic forests/mountains; Rusviet farms/villages; Crimea farms/tundra; Polania villages/mountains. Nordic faction Swim workers only across rivers to any land terrain, never lakes; no mech/character benefit.
grades.observed_answer: Riverwalk lets the character and mechs enter the listed destinations: Rusviet farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Nordic forests and mountains; Polania villages and mountains; Saxony forests and mountains. Nordic Swim applies to workers alone, lets them cross rivers to any land terrain but not lakes, and does not help character/mechs; it gives no lake movement to Nordic mechs.
grades.reader_evidence: Faction ability table lists Riverwalk destinations; Nordic Swim description expressly excludes lakes and character/mechs.
grades.reason: All five Riverwalk terrain pairs/character-mech scope and worker-only Nordic river/not-lake Swim resolved.

grades.question: Which locations become adjacent under Saxony Underpass and Rusviet Township, and which units can use those shortcuts?
grades.expected_answer: Underpass controlled mountains and all tunnels (including own Mine) adjacent for character/mechs. Township controlled villages and Factory adjacent for character/mechs. Not workers; required ability unlocked via deploy.
grades.observed_answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including your Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use either shortcut.
grades.reader_evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township specify locations and character/mech movement.
grades.reason: Saxony controlled mountains+tunnels and Rusviet controlled villages+Factory, character/mech-only adjacency resolved.

grades.question: When does Saxony Disarm apply, how often, and how does Nordic Artillery differ?
grades.expected_answer: Disarm before combat on printed tunnel or own Mine: opponent loses 2 power once per combat, not per unit. Artillery before any combat may pay 1 power to make opponent lose 2, once per combat. Track losses; attacker ability before defender.
grades.observed_answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine: the opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery also applies before combat, but you may pay one power to reduce the opponent’s power by two; it is once per combat, not per unit.
grades.reader_evidence: Disarm and Artillery ability descriptions specify timing, amount, and per-combat frequency.
grades.reason: Saxony tunnel/Mine Disarm versus Nordic paid Artillery, timing/track reductions/once-per-combat resolved.

grades.question: With Rusviet People's Army, how many cards may two mechs and three workers play, and can workers alone fight?
grades.expected_answer: Three cards: one per mech plus one total for at least one worker. Need character/mech; workers alone cannot fight. Ability unlocked.
grades.observed_answer: With two mechs and three workers present, Rusviet may play three combat cards total (one extra card total if at least one worker is present, plus the two participating mechs). Workers alone never fight; a character or mech is required.
grades.reader_evidence: People’s Army: “Two mechs and three workers allow three cards”; workers alone never fight.
grades.reason: Three-card result from two mechs plus worker presence, and character/mech combat requirement resolved.

grades.question: Where may Crimea Wayfare move its character/mechs, and can they enter an active opponent home base?

grades.question: If a character reaches an encounter during Factory bottom Move, can it continue moving, and does the encounter occur before all combats finish?
grades.expected_answer: No character movement again that turn; Factory Move obeys stop rules. Encounter after entire Move and all combats; character must remain there. Bottom Factory Move still triggers normal encounter.
grades.observed_answer: Yes, a character entering an encounter token territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move. Resolve encounters after the whole Move action and all combats, only if the character remains there.
grades.reader_evidence: Move encounter rule and Encounters section; Factory says normal movement/stop restrictions apply.
grades.reason: Both explicitly state that the character cannot move again that turn, including Factory Move, and that encounter resolution waits until all movement and combats are complete, provided the character remains. The opening Yes conflicts with the yes/no polarity of the question, but immediately introduces the explicit correct proposition that the character stops and cannot move again; the substantive rule answer is unambiguous. Independent requested-scope adjudication; no facts borrowed from other answers.

grades.question: What information about coins, combat cards and objectives is public, and is the exact coin total required on request?
grades.expected_answer: Coin holdings not hidden but need not reveal total value; combat card count public, contents secret; may conceal whether cards used in combat until reveal. Objectives secret until revealed.
grades.observed_answer: Combat-card count is public but contents secret; objective contents are secret. Coins are not hidden information, but a player need not reveal their total coin value. During combat players may conceal whether they committed cards until reveal.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup information paragraph.
grades.reason: Coin information/optional total disclosure, combat count versus contents/commitment concealment and objective secrecy resolved.

grades.question: Which things can be exchanged in alliances, are agreements enforceable, and can a payment cancel combat once begun?
grades.expected_answer: Only tangible exchange coins (tournament exception no coin trades for deals/alliances); informal agreements unenforceable. Cannot cancel already initiated combat by negotiation; must fight after Move, though bribes may influence outcome.
grades.observed_answer: Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable in informal, unenforceable agreements; tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances. A payment cannot cancel combat after movement has put units onto opposing units; combat must occur, though bribes may influence the outcome.
grades.reader_evidence: Objectives and agreements: ‘Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable’; agreements unenforceable; negotiation cannot cancel initiated combat.
grades.reason: Only coin exchanges/tournament exception, unenforceable agreements and mandatory initiated combat resolved.

grades.question: State all final-scoring popularity tiers and payouts; do controlled lakes and home bases count, and do leftover single resources score?
grades.expected_answer: 0-6: stars3/territories2/pairs1;7-12:4/3/2;13-18:5/4/3. Lakes count if controlled, home bases never. Factory three total. Sum controlled resources across board and score floor(total/2), no leftover single; workers not resources.
grades.observed_answer: At popularity 0–6, each star pays $3, territory $2, resource pair $1; at 7–12, $4, $3, $2; at 13–18, $5, $4, $3. Controlled lakes count, home bases do not. Only complete pairs score; an odd leftover resource is ignored.
grades.reader_evidence: Final fortune table and scoring paragraph.
grades.reason: All three scoring tiers/rates, lakes/home/Factory, pooled floor pairs/no workers resolved.

grades.question: For adjacent-tunnel, adjacent-encounter and adjacent-lake structure bonuses, how are duplicates, rivers, removed encounters and Mines treated, and what are the payouts?
grades.expected_answer: Count each qualifying adjacent feature once across structures. Rivers do not break adjacency; removed encounter tokens still count printed encounter. Mine not tunnel for tile. Adjacent tunnels count1=$2,2-3=$4,4-5=$6,6=$9; lakes/encounters1=$2,2-3=$4,4-5=$6,6-7=$9; zero=$0.
grades.observed_answer: For adjacency tiles, count unique features once across all structures; rivers do not break adjacency. Encounters count at printed locations even after their tokens are removed. Tunnel counts are unique printed tunnel territories, not Mines. Lakes count unique lakes. Payout for each of these three tiles: 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; tunnel 6 $9; lakes/encounters 6–7 $9. Zero qualifying features scores zero.
grades.reader_evidence: Structure bonus table and following rules specify unique counts, removed encounters, printed tunnels, river rule and payouts.
grades.reason: Three adjacency tile features/unique counting/rivers/removed encounter/Mine exception and exact payout ranges resolved.

grades.question: For structures on tunnels, structures in a row, and structures on farms/tundras, what qualifies and what are the payouts?
grades.expected_answer: On printed tunnels not Mine:1=$2,2=$4,3-4=$6. Longest continuous straight line only, rivers do not break:1=$2,2=$4,3=$6,4=$9. Farms+tundras combined number with structures:1=$2,2=$4,3=$6,4=$9. Zero=$0. Bonus regardless territory control.
grades.observed_answer: Structures on tunnels counts printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. Structures in a row scores only the longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break it: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Structures on farms/tundras counts qualifying structures combined: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
grades.reader_evidence: Structure bonus table entries for these three tiles.
grades.reason: Printed-tunnel versus Mine, longest continuous straight row/rivers, combined farm+tundra and each exact payout resolved.

grades.question: In combat on a lake, does a winning attacker lose popularity for workers carried by the defeated mech?
grades.expected_answer: Yes one popularity per forced-retreat worker even carried on lake; retreat with mech to home base by default (Nordic Seaworthy permits adjacent-lake retreat). Polania unlocked Camaraderie exception after combat.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity for each enemy worker forced to retreat, including a worker carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat step 5 explicitly includes workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
grades.reason: Winning lake attacker loses popularity for carried defeated workers, normal retreat and named faction exceptions resolved.

grades.question: Does placing a popularity star protect current popularity or its scoring tier, and can two factions both star the same achievement?
grades.expected_answer: Star itself permanent, popularity may fall and final payout uses current tier. Other factions may also place same goal; no blocking.
grades.observed_answer: No. A placed star is permanent, but current popularity determines final scoring, so a popularity star does not protect the current popularity level or scoring tier. Another player's star never blocks the same goal; each player's achievement may be awarded.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars paragraph: ‘A placed star is permanent even if power/popularity later drops; current popularity still determines final scoring’; ‘Other players’ stars never block a goal.’
grades.reason: Permanent star versus mutable current scoring tier, other factions sharing goal resolved.

grades.question: How are Faction Mats and Player Mats assigned, and in what relative faction order should players sit? Why does that seating matter for recruit bonuses?
grades.expected_answer: Randomly shuffle the Faction Mats and Player Mats and deal one of each to each player. Players sit near their faction home bases, with the clockwise order from the top Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, using the factions in the game. Recruit ongoing bonuses respond to the player and their immediate left/right neighbors, so those neighbors follow the seating arrangement.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 20: ONGOING BONUS and PLAYER ORDER
grades.observed_answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions clockwise in board order: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. This determines immediate left/right neighbors whose corresponding bottom actions can trigger ongoing recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup steps 2–3 and Ongoing recruits neighbor-trigger rule.
grades.reason: Random mat assignment, complete prescribed clockwise faction order and immediate-neighbor recruit consequence resolved.

grades.question: For movement, what distinguishes a river from a lake, and from which surrounding land territories can a unit with a lake-movement ability enter the lake?
grades.expected_answer: A river lies on the border between two land territories. A lake comprises an entire territory hex and extends from that hex to any adjacent shoreline. A unit with the appropriate lake-movement ability can move onto it from any of the surrounding territories shown by that shoreline; crossing permission for a river alone does not grant entry to lakes.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 11: RIVERS AND LAKES; RIVER; LAKE; illustrated example
grades.observed_answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
grades.reader_evidence: Move terrain paragraph defines river/lake and lake entry.
grades.reason: River as land border, lake as entire hex extending to adjacent shores, lake-ability entry and river-only insufficiency resolved.

grades.question: When you draw an encounter card, may you keep it private? What must you show or read aloud to the other players?
grades.expected_answer: The encounter card is shown to all players when drawn. Show its artwork and read the capitalized thematic text aloud, then read through its costs and benefits and choose an option. The rules do not require reading every option aloud.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 24, ENCOUNTERS: Show the art to the other players and read the thematic text (the text in all caps) out loud.

grades.reader_evidence: Encounters: ‘Show the encounter card to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud.’
grades.reason: Encounter card/art public and capitalized thematic text read aloud resolved; reading every option aloud is not required.

grades.question: Is there any limit to the number of your units or resource tokens that may occupy one territory?
grades.expected_answer: There is no per-territory limit on same-faction units or resource tokens. This does not remove the separate one-structure-per-territory restriction.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p11 NO LIMIT: no limit to same-faction units on a territory
Rulebook PDF p13 NO LIMIT: any number of resource tokens or workers can be on a territory
grades.observed_answer: There is no limit to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
grades.reader_evidence: Control, resources and home bases: ‘No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.’
grades.reason: No per-territory limit on same-faction units or resource tokens resolved; separate structure limit remains.

grades.question: Must the next player wait until the current player has finished every bottom-row decision, or when may the next turn begin?
grades.expected_answer: The next clockwise player may begin when the current player starts or is finalizing a bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure or recruit to gain. The ordinary alternative is to start after the current turn is complete. This overlap does not reverse the stated recruit-bonus priority or the immediate game-end rule.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p10 GAMEPLAY, paragraph beginning After you have completed your turn

grades.observed_answer: The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure or recruit to gain.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: ‘After the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, the next clockwise player may begin their turn while the current player decides…’

grades.question: After taking the selected top-row or bottom-row action, may you pay its cost again to take that same action a second time in the same turn?
grades.expected_answer: No. Each action may be taken only once during the turn; paying the full cost again does not permit repeating it.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p10 GAMEPLAY, once-per-action restriction
grades.observed_answer: No. You may take each section's top action once and then its bottom action once; you cannot return to the top action after the bottom. A section cannot be taken twice in one turn. Rusviet may repeat a section from last turn, including its Factory card, which is not a second action within the same turn.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure specifies top once, bottom once and no return; Rusviet may repeat a section from last turn.

grades.question: What can you gain from the normal, unupgraded Move action if you choose not to move any units?
grades.expected_answer: You may choose to gain $1 instead of moving units. Moving and gaining the listed coins are alternative choices.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p11 MOVE: move units OR GAIN COIN(S)
grades.observed_answer: You may alternatively gain $1 from the normal unupgraded Move action.
grades.reader_evidence: Top-row Move: ‘Alternatively gain $1.’
grades.reason: Normal Move coin alternative gives $1 instead of movement resolved.

grades.question: May a worker already on the board be returned to your Player Mat to cover a Produce cost again, including after it retreats?
grades.expected_answer: No. Once on the board, a worker never returns to the Player Mat. A forced retreat puts it on the home base, not back on its Produce rectangle.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p13 WORKERS ARE PERMANENT
Rulebook PDF p23 LOSER: retreat all units to home base
grades.observed_answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat. A worker retreating to its home base does not return to the Player Mat either, so it cannot cover a Produce cost again.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce: ‘Workers never return to the Player Mat’; forced worker retreat goes to home base.
grades.reason: Workers never return to Player Mat/cover Produce costs; retreat destination remains home base resolved.

grades.question: May you initiate combat when you have zero power, zero popularity, or both?

source_references: Rulebook PDF p22 NO REQUIREMENTS and SELECT POWER
grades.observed_answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power, zero popularity, or both.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat: ‘You may attack with zero power/popularity.’
grades.reason: Zero power, zero popularity or both do not bar combat initiation resolved.

grades.question: After a faction other than Saxony has already earned its two combat-victory stars, may it still initiate and win further combats?
grades.expected_answer: Yes. The limit restricts further combat stars, not participation or winning. It may continue fighting but gains no additional combat-victory stars.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p23 LIMITED STARS AND GAME END
grades.observed_answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit, though you cannot place more ordinary combat stars beyond the two-star limit.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat: ‘You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit.’
grades.reason: Ordinary two-combat-star cap limits further stars, not future combats or winning resolved.

grades.question: For a faction without Meander, may you decline to choose an option after drawing an encounter, choose an option you cannot afford, or decline some of the chosen option benefits?

source_references: Rulebook PDF p24 REQUIRED COST AND OPTIONAL BENEFIT

grades.reason: Non-Meander encounter requires one affordable option/full printed cost, but benefits may be partly or wholly declined resolved.

grades.question: Do combatants select their Power Dials in turn order, and when are the dials and selected combat cards revealed?
grades.expected_answer: They select dial power simultaneously and secretly, then reveal both Power Dials and any selected combat cards simultaneously. Attacker-first resolution of combat mech abilities does not make the power selection or reveal sequential.
grades.observed_answer: No turn-order selection: combatants simultaneously and secretly choose their dials and optional cards. They reveal simultaneously.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 1–3: ‘simultaneously and secretly choose’; ‘Reveal simultaneously.’
grades.reason: Simultaneous secret dial selection and simultaneous dial/card reveal, distinct from attacker-first abilities resolved.

grades.question: When taking a bottom-row action, what must you announce to the other players, and why?
grades.expected_answer: You must announce that you are taking the bottom-row action, so the players immediately to your left and right can check their Recruit Ongoing Bonuses.
grades.observed_answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Bottom-row actions: ‘Announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.’
grades.reason: Mandatory bottom-action announcement lets immediate neighbors check ongoing recruits resolved.

grades.question: After you achieve a star goal, may you decline or delay placing that star to avoid ending the game? How does this differ from holding a completed objective card unrevealed?
grades.expected_answer: An earned star must be placed on the appropriate achievement immediately; it cannot be declined or delayed to avoid ending the game. You may instead wait to reveal a completed objective, provided you still satisfy it when you reveal it; when you reveal it, place the star.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p27 PLACING STARS: when you achieve one of these goals, you must place a star
Rulebook PDF p2 TRIUMPH TRACK: as soon as you complete a requirement
Rulebook PDF p26 OBJECTIVES: may wait to reveal, requirements must hold at reveal
grades.observed_answer: No. Place a star as soon as its goal is achieved; it cannot be declined or delayed, and the sixth star immediately ends play. A completed objective is different: you may wait to reveal it, but when revealed on your turn you must meet all requirements at that moment.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars: ‘Place a star as soon as you achieve’; Sixth star ends immediately. Objectives: ‘You may wait’ to reveal.
grades.reason: Earned threshold star placement mandatory/immediate; completed objective reveal may wait while requirements hold resolved.

grades.question: Before any faction or mech ability provides an exception, may a character, mech or worker move across a river or onto a lake?
grades.expected_answer: No. By default, none of the three unit types may cross rivers or move onto lakes. An applicable special ability is required to override the relevant restriction.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 5: TYPES OF UNITS: all three unit types can move around the board, not over rivers or onto lakes by default.
Rulebook PDF p. 11: RIVERS AND LAKES: By default, units may not move across rivers or onto lakes; some mech abilities break the rule.
grades.observed_answer: Normally no character, mech or worker may cross rivers or enter lakes. The summary then describes faction/mech ability exceptions.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: ‘Units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes.’
grades.reason: All three unit types face default river/lake movement prohibition absent applicable ability resolved.

grades.question: After placing an enlisted recruit on a Recruit One-Time Bonus space on your Faction Mat, may you move that recruit token later to free the space for another recruit?
grades.expected_answer: No. An enlisted recruit token remains on its chosen Faction Mat space permanently and cannot be moved. You cannot free an occupied one-time bonus space by relocating that token.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 20: ONE-TIME BONUS: place the recruit on any open Recruit One-Time Bonus space; the token remains there permanently and cannot be moved.
grades.observed_answer: No. The recruit is placed permanently on an open one-time recruit bonus on the Faction Mat and cannot later move.
grades.reader_evidence: Enlist: ‘put it permanently’; ‘It cannot later move.’
grades.reason: Enlisted recruit remains permanently on chosen Faction Mat space; cannot relocate to reopen space resolved.

grades.question: May a mech or worker resolve an encounter or remove its encounter token merely by entering that territory?
grades.expected_answer: No. Only characters trigger encounters. A mech or worker entering a territory does not resolve its encounter or remove the encounter token; it remains for a character.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p.5, TYPES OF UNITS: characters can have encounters; other units have different roles.
Rulebook PDF p.24, ENCOUNTERS: Only characters will trigger an encounter. Token removal occurs when resolving the character-triggered encounter.
Rulebook PDF p.31, ENCOUNTERS: Only characters may have encounters.
grades.observed_answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering the territory does not resolve it or remove the token.
grades.reader_evidence: Encounters: ‘Only a character triggers an encounter.’
grades.reason: Only character triggers encounter; mech/worker entry does not resolve/remove token resolved.

grades.question: While you control the territory containing your Mill, how does it affect the number of territories you may Produce on and the output there, including when no actual worker is present?
grades.expected_answer: The Mill territory may count as an extra bonus territory in addition to the normal territories selected for Produce. The Mill produces as if it were one worker, so it can produce even with no actual worker there. Any actual workers on its territory may also produce.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p18, MILL: Whenever you take the Produce action, the territory with the Mill may count as an extra (bonus) territory for production. The Mill will produce as if it were a worker. If there are actual workers on the Mill territory, they may also produce resources.
grades.observed_answer: While controlled, the Mill adds one bonus Produce territory in addition to the normal selected territories. The Mill itself counts as one producing worker, and each actual worker there also produces normally. With no actual worker, the Mill can still produce one terrain-table token, provided the territory is controlled.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce: controlled Mill provides an additional territory; Mill counts as a worker; can produce without an actual worker. Control rule excludes uncontrolled Mill production.
grades.reason: Controlled Mill adds bonus production territory, produces as one worker without actual worker, and actual workers may also produce resolved.

grades.question: What presence establishes control of a territory, and do resources alone preserve your control after your last unit leaves a territory where you have no structure?
grades.expected_answer: You control a territory with at least one of your units, or with your structure and no enemy units. Resources are not units and do not establish control. If your last unit leaves and you have no structure there, you no longer control that territory or the resources left there; those resources cannot be spent by you unless you regain control.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p4, CONTROL: control requires at least one unit or a structure with no enemy units; only one player controls a territory at a time.
Rulebook PDF p4, RESOURCES: resource tokens remain on the board and may be spent only from territories currently controlled.
Rulebook PDF p29, EVERY TERRITORY CONTROLLED and EVERY 2 RESOURCES CONTROLLED; PDF p31, END-GAME SCORING.
grades.observed_answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish or preserve control after your last unit leaves if you have no structure.
grades.reader_evidence: Control, resources and home bases: control is by unit or structure with no enemy unit; resources stay on board but are not listed as control.
grades.reason: Control needs unit or own structure without enemy units; resources alone do not maintain control/spending after last unit leaves resolved.

grades.question: Which resource is used to pay for the Build action, and which is used to pay for the Enlist action?
grades.expected_answer: Build uses wood. Enlist uses food; the amount required is the exposed cost on the corresponding Player Mat action.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p10, GAMEPLAY, exposed red-box costs
grades.observed_answer: Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
grades.reader_evidence: Bottom-row actions: ‘Upgrade — oil’; ‘Deploy — metal’; ‘Build — wood’; ‘Enlist — food.’
grades.reason: Build is paid in wood and Enlist in food; exact amount follows exposed Player Mat cost resolved.
